deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 66–68): Grothendieck is setting up a 'dévissage' of a stratified space or topos X. The strata are indexed by a poset I. Each stratum has an open part X_i^*. For a stratum X_i and a stratum X_j with i ≤ j there are tubular neighbourhoods V_{ij} of X_i in X_j and 'deleted' neighbourhoods V^*_{ij} = V_{ij} minus X_i^*. These carry three types of maps:
- X_i^* → V_{ij}, the inclusion of the stratum into its tube, a homotopy equivalence via the retraction;
- V^*_{ij} → V_{ij}, the inclusion of the deleted tube;
- V^*_{ij} → X_j^*, the inclusion of the deleted tube into the higher stratum.

On the previous page he grades I by a dimension function d : I → Z satisfying (24): d(j) = d(i)+1 exactly when j is an immediate successor of i. He then forms coproducts over each degree, X_m^*, V_{m,m+1} and V^*_{m,m+1}, giving a 'staircase' zig-zag (26): X_m^* → V_{m,m+1} ← V^*_{m,m+1} → X^*_{m+1}.

This page records the dual convention, a codimension function with d(j) = d(i) − 1 when j succeeds i. One then uses V_{d,d−1} and V^*_{d,d−1} instead of V_{d,d+1} and V^*_{d,d+1}. The staircase (27) runs from the deepest stratum X_n^* (codimension n) down to the open dense stratum X_0^*:
X_n^* → V_{n,n−1} ← V^*_{n,n−1} → X^*_{n−1} → V_{n−1,n−2} ← V^*_{n−1,n−2} → X^*_{n−2} → … → X_1^* → V_{1,0} ← V^*_{1,0} → X_0^*.

The purpose shows on the next page, the 'Théorème de recollement des topos (1ère version)'. X should be recovered as the 2-limit of the diagram of topoi (strata, tubes, deleted tubes) indexed by the category Ĩ built from successor pairs. A stratified space would thus be glued from its strata along tubular neighbourhoods and links. This is an early form of the now-standard description of a stratified homotopy type by strata plus homotopy links, i.e. exit paths.
errors: Slip in the diagram: the target of V^*_{n−1,n−2} is written X^*_{n−1}; it should be X^*_{n−2}.
In the opening parenthesis the intended condition is d(j) = d(i) − 1 if j is a successor of i (codimension convention). The written form is garbled.

Mathematical gap (affecting the next page's theorem as stated): the staircase (27), and the diagram of type Ĩ, use only pairs (i, j) with j an immediate successor of i. For a general stratification, a stratum X_k can approach X_i directly even when k is not a successor of i; think of the cone on a stratified space with a 1-dimensional stratum. The deleted neighbourhood V^*_{ik} and the higher link data for flags i<j<k are then not encoded by successor data. Modern exodromy results use the full exit-path ∞-category, i.e. links of all chains, not just length-one successor steps. Grothendieck seems aware of this: the margin on the next page adds 'pourvu que en un sens précis…'.
Flattening the diagram into one linear chain via coproducts over degrees forgets which pieces of V_{m,m−1} go to which pieces of X^*_{m−1}. As a gluing datum it is only a schematic picture.

ideas.what: Grading the poset of strata by a dimension or codimension function with successor condition (24), and forming degree-wise coproducts of strata, tubes and deleted tubes, giving a staircase zig-zag diagram
ideas.modern_name: Graded / ranked stratification poset; zig-zag of strata and homotopy links
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory (Thom, Mather); homotopy links: Quinn 1988
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses dévissage of stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods, but not this diagram

ideas.what: Recovering the stratified space/topos as a 2-limit of the topoi of strata, tubular neighbourhoods and deleted neighbourhoods (motivating diagram for the next page's recollement theorem)
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/exodromy of stratified spaces from strata and links; recollement of ∞-topoi along links
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson / Treumann (exit paths); Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; Barwick–Glasman–Haine (Exodromy, 2018); Haine; Douteau
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 sketches the idea of a 'théorie de dévissage' of stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods; no precise theorem published

missed.claim: This page only switches from a dimension to a codimension convention and draws the staircase diagram. Its substantive content is a picture of the decomposition of a stratified space into strata glued along tubes and links, as a diagram of topoi. That decomposition is now well developed (exodromy, Haine's link decompositions), so nothing here is new beyond documenting that Grothendieck pursued it c. 1981.
missed.quote: (Cas d'une fonction codimension) X^*_n → V_{n,n−1} ← V^*_{n,n−1} ↓ X^*_{n−1} … X^*_1 → V_{1,0} ← V^*_{1,0} ↓ X^*_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck aiming at a 'stratified recollement' theorem expressing a stratified topos as a 2-limit of elementary topoi along tubular neighbourhoods. This predates the ∞-categorical exodromy literature, but the page itself contains no result.

deep.surprise_reason: A notational and diagrammatic page (codimension variant of the staircase diagram). The underlying idea of gluing strata along tubular neighbourhoods and links is interesting historically and anticipates exodromy-type results. But it is sketched in the Esquisse, and the page adds no theorem or construction beyond the diagram.
transcription_corrections: Opening parenthesis should read roughly '(d(j) = d(i)−1 si j successeur de i)', not '(dim = j−1 si j = ... de i)'.

Line 3 should read 'on considère des V_{d,d−1}, V^*_{d,d−1} au lieu des V_{d,d+1}, V^*_{d,d+1}'. The transcription's 'V_{d,d−1}, V^λ_{d,d−1}' misreads the second pair, which has indices d,d+1 and a star.
Third line of the diagram: the manuscript writes X^*_{n−1}, but it is evidently a slip for X^*_{n−2}.
The '(27)' label is struck through at the top and rewritten in the left margin beside the diagram; the dash '—' indicates the elided middle of the staircase.
